chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: The Newark pit orchestra for silent films
summary: The pit band, led by violinist Floyd Hickman with Ted Nixon on trombone, were virtuosos who played heavy classical music for silent pictures, giving Butler broad experience.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So you were playing in a lot of keys.

Oh, yes, because we had to play the music for the silent moving pictures. We had a -- we played all that music and it was called William Tell's 'Overture' and great they had a violinist; his name was Floyd Hickman. But all these people were masters,

These were virtuosos: a boy named Ted Nixon, trombone. They had a bass man, played cello and all these things. I forget his name and there's another boy, the drummer, they were percussions, these was a pit band. A man named Slim Henderson. And Henderson could sit right there and play and write the names like that, but Hickman was the orchestra leader and so and so and that's all he said.

You get up there and do your act, and he'd write

it out for you, and so -- and I was getting all that heavy music and that give me experience and now-- so the 101 Ranch came to New Jersey, Newark, and I became a friend with Eddie Durham and all his brothers, we became very staunch friends.
